problem: Existing embodied navigation tasks (ObjectNav, VLN) need a fixed category set or granular step-by-step instructions, and are validated mostly in small household scenes. They do not cover signage-driven wayfinding in large-scale indoor spaces such as hospitals and airports, and prior signage work is rule-based or modular rather than end-to-end.
motivation: Humans navigate novel public buildings by following signage, which acts as an implicit, dynamic instruction set. Signage is sparse and its hints change along the route, so an agent must ground each hint in the current view and remember earlier hints when none is visible. No task or dataset exists for learning this end to end.
key_idea: Define the SignNav task and LSI-Dataset, and train a Spatial-Temporal Aware Transformer (START) that grounds the signage arrow hint into the current RGB-D view (hint-initialised CLS token) and reasons over a window of past states to output low-level actions.
insight: Both modules are needed. Spatial-only reaches 0.47 SR and temporal-only 0.39 SR on val-unseen, while combined they reach 0.72 SR (no DAgger). DAgger adds a further 8 points of SR on unseen scenes. Depth-only input beats RGB-D (0.77 vs 0.72 SR val-unseen), which the authors attribute to depth being robust to texture and illumination shifts.
method: Task formulation: a POMDP with discrete actions (forward 0.25 m, turn ±15°, stop); observations are RGB-D plus a cropped directional-arrow hint h_t and its bounding box b_t; the policy conditions on history H_t.

LSI-Dataset: 20 large scanned scenes (hospitals, offices; avg ~1000 m²) from Matterport3D, Gibson and Stanford scans. Arrow-only signage is injected procedurally in Blender at decision points, and episodes are generated by Poisson-disk waypoint graphs, Dijkstra paths and spline smoothing, with arrow direction derived from trajectory curvature.

Input embeddings: separate lightweight CNNs for RGB and depth are fused with LayerNorm. The hint embedding combines an ImageNet ResNet-50 feature of the crop with normalized bbox coordinates and area, each projected.

Spatial-Aware Transformer: ViT-B/32-style over the fused visual patches, with the [CLS] token replaced by the hint embedding so attention weights patches by hint relevance. It outputs a spatial embedding and a hint-token output.

Temporal-Aware Transformer: BERT-like, 6 layers, 6 heads, hidden size 768. It takes a fixed-length window of past state embeddings (pooled spatial embedding plus action embedding) and the current features, and an MLP head outputs the action distribution.
Training: teacher-forcing imitation with inflection-weighted cross-entropy, then 10 DAgger iterations of 100 epochs each (lr 1e-5, batch 12, 6 RTX4090).
Real-world pipeline: Lite2 robot with a RealSense D435i, DepthAnything-V2 for depth, Qwen3-8B to parse hints and decide termination, and inference on a remote GPU at 0.5 Hz.

setting.backbone: START: ViT-B/32-style spatial transformer + BERT-like temporal transformer, ResNet-50 hint encoder, lightweight CNNs (trained; ResNet-50 ImageNet-pretrained)
setting.training_data: LSI-Dataset train split: 16 scenes, 8000 episodes (avg ~10 m) with oracle actions, plus DAgger-aggregated on-policy data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus cropped signage-arrow hint image and its bounding box
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 15°, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (LSI-Dataset built from Matterport3D/Gibson/Stanford scans with Blender-injected signage)
setting.privileged: Hints (arrow crops and bboxes) are provided as structured input, assumed detected; in real-world deployment they are parsed by Qwen3-8B. No map or pose.

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (0.80) in the paper. Values are kept as printed, not converted to percent. The task is the paper's own benchmark, not a canonical one. The 40-200 m trajectory RMSE study is on selected scenes (0.24-0.28 m).
results: START gets 0.80 SR / 0.74 NDTW on val-unseen, versus ViNT (retrained) at 0.68 / 0.69, the rule-based method at 0.67 / 0.73, and the Qwen3 VLM-based agent at 0.30 / 0.54. Trajectory RMSE stays around 0.25-0.28 m for routes of 40-200 m, and the model ran on a real robot without a map.
limitations: Signage is abstracted to arrow-only hints with no text, so OCR and semantic matching are not addressed. Hints are assumed to be detected and cropped upstream, and the real-world system relies on Qwen3-8B to parse them.
The dataset is simulated, with procedurally injected signage on 20 scanned scenes, and the val-unseen split has only 4 scenes. The real-world evaluation is qualitative, with no quantitative results.
Baselines are weak or ad hoc: the VLM baseline is a custom Qwen3 agent with no released prompt, and the rule-based baseline scoring higher on val-unseen than val-seen is left unexplained.
